proposedSourceChecks.assessment: Three-page Executive Order N-9-26 was read. It is effective immediately; it directs specified agency implementation deadlines (May 1 and December 1, 2027) and a November 16, 2026 recommendations deadline. The proposed kill-switch, onsite verifier, and expanded incident-reporting requirements are recommendations for potential amendments, not current mandates.

The September 18 EFF response was read. It supports the order's existence and records EFF's view that loss-of-control reporting and third-party investigations merit attention, while identifying effectiveness of kill switches as active research. It is commentary, not proof that the proposed measures are enacted or effective.

The committee's September 16 release records House passage of H.R. 9340, the Ratepayer Protection Act, 417-3. It describes a requirement that state regulators consider large-load standards for data centers above 100 MW. It does not establish Senate passage, presidential signature, or a current nationwide payment obligation.

Apple's June 10, 2024 PCC technical account was read. It describes Apple's claimed architecture and its explicit distinction from ordinary cloud protections. It does not document a September 2026 feature change or settle EFF's normative critique of cloud TEEs.

The captured Nature report names the underlying Science paper (10.1126/science.aeg6779) and describes a virtual biotech using up to 37,075 agents. It also says the drug-discovery predictions were not validated through experiments or clinical trials. The underlying study still requires complete examination before any reporting beyond a bounded lead.

The captured Nature report names a Cell paper (189, 5980-5994.e8) and a separate Nature Biotechnology study. It describes specialist ageing models and benchmarks, but says interpretation of biological-age clocks remains unsettled. The complete underlying work and exact scope must be inspected before any health or longevity implication is reported.

proposedLeadDispositions.productionLimits: Do not say a new kill-switch, onsite verifier, or amended critical-incident rule is in force. Retain EO deadlines and EFF's clearly attributed critique.
proposedLeadDispositions.outstandingWork: Bind exact current California statutory references and complete ordinary producer, independent review, admission, and reader-contract checks.

proposedLeadDispositions.event: House passage of H.R. 9340, the Ratepayer Protection Act
proposedLeadDispositions.reader-safe-frame: The House vote would put a state-regulator consideration standard before large data-center costs; it is a legislative step, not a live national utility-bill rule.
proposedLeadDispositions.productionLimits: State the 417-3 House vote and 100 MW committee-described threshold with attribution. Do not claim enactment, guaranteed rate relief, or a uniform obligation until the bill's later legislative status is verified.

proposedLeadDispositions.event: EFF analysis of cloud TEEs and encrypted messaging
proposedLeadDispositions.reason: The full EFF opinion and Apple historical documentation are accessible, while the Meta whitepaper capture is metadata only. There is no verified new provider feature, affected-service scope, current user setting, or independent technical assessment that would justify a general-reader product/privacy story.
proposedLeadDispositions.nextAction: Recover current service-specific documentation and an independent technical assessment; preserve the distinction between end-to-end encryption and cloud-TEE processing.

proposedLeadDispositions.event: Virtual Biotech research and proposed lung-cancer therapeutic strategy
proposedLeadDispositions.reason: Nature reporting, Stanford's institutional account, and the project site support a research lead only. Their language differs in emphasis: Nature says the predictions were not experimentally or clinically validated, while Stanford says a later independently built therapy was validated in trials. The underlying Science study and the exact evidence chain for the latter institutional wording were not inspected.
proposedLeadDispositions.nextAction: Read the Science paper in full, recover exact source for Stanford's later-validation statement, reconcile the claims, and preserve the boundary between hypothesis generation and clinical benefit.

proposedLeadDispositions.event: AI system and benchmarks for ageing research
proposedLeadDispositions.reason: The Nature report is readable but points to underlying Cell and Nature Biotechnology research not inspected in full. It expressly preserves uncertainty about what biological-age changes mean, so it cannot support a health, rejuvenation, or clinical-effect claim.
proposedLeadDispositions.nextAction: Recover/read the primary papers and an independent domain-expert account; specify model tasks, evaluation population, and what the work does not demonstrate.
